clue.text: Old money was in operation in soccer team

indicators.note: 'in' says one piece sits inside the soccer team's abbreviation

parts.note: FC stands for Football Club
a machine that ran was in operation

explanation.surface: Someone recalls cash a football club once operated with.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the currency of France and Belgium before the euro replaced it, so it is old money.

clue.text: Stormy sea — for me — is frightful

indicators.note: stormy means turbulent, so the letters are tossed about

explanation.surface: A sailor fears a stormy sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fearsome inspires fear, so it is frightening, frightful.

clue.text: Poet university engaged in a study

indicators.note: engaged in means occupying a place within the other words

parts.note: a den is a small private study

explanation.surface: A poet employed at a university works in a study.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden was an Anglo-American poet of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Male home help grabbing iron to do for beetle

parts.note: a cock is a male bird

indicators.note: grabbing means the home help holds the iron symbol inside

parts.note: a char is a British cleaning lady
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A male cleaner seizes an iron to kill a beetle.
explanation.walkthrough: A char (charwoman) is a British cleaner who 'does for' a household, hence 'to do for'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockchafer, or maybug, is a large European beetle.

clue.text: What could be best for centrepiece of meal?

definitions.text: What could be best for centrepiece of meal?

indicators.note: 'could be' hints that these letters might become something else once rearranged
the centrepiece of a word is its middle letters, here the two in the middle of 'meal'

explanation.surface: A host wonders what would be the best main dish for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centrepiece of meal' looks like part of the definition but also supplies the letters EA. The whole clue is the definition: the traditional British Sunday dinner is built around this joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint of roasted beef is the classic main dish of a traditional British Sunday dinner.

clue.text: Controls dog, say, around college? Go over again

parts.note: reins are what control a horse

indicators.note: around means the pet word surrounds the college abbreviation

parts.note: a dog is an example of a pet

explanation.surface: Someone controls a dog being walked around a college.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinspect is to examine once more, to check over a second time.

clue.text: Cancel article on Northern Line after intervention by head of Underground

indicators.note: an intervention comes between, so a letter goes inside the article and abbreviations

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: London's Northern Line service is cancelled when the head of the Underground steps in.
explanation.walkthrough: The Northern Line is a London Underground line, but here it is two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a contract or marriage is to declare it void, to cancel it.

clue.text: Long journey ends in disappointment for the monk

indicators.note: ends in means take the final letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A monk's pilgrimage ends in disappointment.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is an arduous journey, often on foot.

clue.text: Bolting heating component will involve a little work

indicators.note: will involve means the heating part encloses the work abbreviation

parts.note: an element is the heating part of a kettle or oven
op, short for opus, is a little word for a work

explanation.surface: Fixing a heating part with bolts will take a little work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolting' reads as fastening with bolts, but it means running off.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloping is running away secretly to marry, a kind of bolting.

clue.text: More or less shrewd in demeanour? On the contrary

indicators.note: in points to one word being placed within another
on the contrary flips the order the first half suggests, so demeanour goes into shrewd

parts.note: fly is British slang for shrewd or knowing
an air is a manner or demeanour

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone's manner looks shrewd, then a contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half alone would put the shrewd word inside the demeanour word; 'On the contrary' tells you to do the opposite. 'Fly' meaning shrewd is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairly means moderately, to some degree, which is roughly more or less.

clue.text: Carrying away bond in sale

indicators.note: 'in' places the bond's abbreviation within the word for a sale

parts.note: an auction is a sale by bidding
BD is the financial abbreviation for a bond

explanation.surface: Someone reads about a bond being sold off at a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Abduction is the taking away of a person by force, a carrying off.

clue.text: Iconic symbol that is backed after intervention by second judge

indicators.note: an intervention puts something in between, so the two other pieces go inside
backed means the abbreviation for 'that is' runs from right to left

parts.note: i.e. (id est) means that is
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: An instruction about reversing something once a second judge steps in.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small pictograms used in texts, literally icons, so iconic symbol describes them well.

clue.text: Keep expecting to get lost in the main

definitions.text: Keep expecting to get lost in the main

parts.words: Keep expecting to get lost in the main
parts.note: a keep is a castle's stronghold; the main is the sea, and this one on the beach is built expecting the tide to wash it away

explanation.surface: Sounds like advice to persist despite expecting failure in general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' reads as the verb 'continue' and 'the main' as 'mostly', but a keep is a fortified tower and the main is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A play fortress made on the beach is doomed to be swept away by the incoming tide.

clue.text: Corporation curtailed alarm

indicators.note: curtailed means having the tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: corporation is an old jocular word for a paunch or pot belly

explanation.surface: A company's alarm system has been cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a business, but it is the dated humorous word for a big stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringing device that warns people, like a fire or door alarm, is a common kind of alarm.

clue.text: Nicks sitar badly? Such language in India

definitions.note: an adjectival definition: language of this kind, relating to the ancient Indian tongue

indicators.note: badly means the letters are handled poorly and jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone damages a sitar, which draws a scolding in India.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective describes things relating to the classical Indic tongue of Hindu scripture.

clue.text: Hard to avoid network discerning some information…

indicators.note: to avoid means the hard abbreviation must be left out of the network word

parts.note: a mesh is a network of threads
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
sage means wise, discerning

explanation.surface: Someone discerning steers clear of the network to find information.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on with an ellipsis into 16 across, but each clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A communication sent to someone carries a piece of news or data, some information.

clue.text: One guides cattle, a substantial number with tail docked

parts.note: steers are young castrated bulls, cattle

indicators.note: docking a tail cuts off the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: many means a substantial number

explanation.surface: A drover guides cattle, a good number with docked tails.
explanation.definitionFit: A steersman guides a boat by its helm.

clue.text: …favoured involving network to supply orbiter

indicators.note: involving means wrapping around another piece

parts.note: a pet is a favoured one, as in teacher's pet
LAN is a local area network

explanation.surface: A favoured network is used to supply a satellite.
explanation.definitionFit: A world such as Mars or Venus travels round the sun, so it is something that orbits.

clue.text: Turned up with normal throbbing and unknown quantity affecting the lungs

indicators.note: turned means the word 'up' is flipped over
throbbing means pulsing, so the letters are disturbed

parts.note: y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A doctor notes a normal pulse turning up an unknown chest problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' gives PU, 'throbbing' rearranges NORMAL into LMONAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulmonary is the medical adjective meaning relating to the lungs.

clue.text: Some wine is mostly rubbish

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter is kept

parts.note: crud is slang for rubbish or filth

explanation.surface: A wine critic dismisses a bottle as largely rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A cru is a vineyard or its wine of recognised quality, as in grand cru.

clue.text: Girl, initially no longer missing Edward, kept controlled

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word before

parts.note: once you are over someone you no longer miss them
Ned is a pet name for Edward

explanation.surface: A girl no longer misses Edward, who kept her in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing' looks like loss of letters, but 'no longer missing' is one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To govern a thing is to keep it under control or regulate it.

clue.text: Scoff after remarkable thrashing

indicators.note: after says the word for scoff comes behind the slang word

parts.note: def is slang for excellent, remarkable
to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: Someone mocks after a remarkable beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' looks like 'mock' but is the British informal verb for eating greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrashing in a match is a heavy loss, a beating, a rout.

clue.text: Vibrant hotels seen around old country

indicators.note: seen around means the shuffled hotel letters surround the old abbreviation
vibrant means lively, quivering, so the letters move about

explanation.surface: Lively hotels surround an old country town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vibrant' rearranges HOTELS into LESTHO, and 'seen around' puts it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a landlocked kingdom in southern Africa, completely surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Welshman, cunning, interrupting last two-thirds of meeting

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of another word
keeping two of three letters means the first one is dropped

parts.note: an AGM is an annual general meeting
wily means cunning

explanation.surface: A sly Welshman disrupts the end of a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Gwilym is the Welsh form of William, a man's name in Wales.

clue.text: Controversy backing Duke's command

indicators.note: backing means the synonym for controversy is read from right to left

parts.note: a row is a quarrel or controversy
D is the abbreviation for Duke

explanation.surface: A controversy surrounds support for a duke's order.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving the word means issuing an order, as in 'just say the word'.

clue.text: Put in difficult position, our entering nick is worthy of respect

indicators.note: put in places the rest of the construction inside the word for a difficult position

parts.note: to be in a hole is to be in a difficult position

indicators.note: entering says 'our' goes inside the word for nick

parts.note: to nick is to nab, catch or arrest

explanation.surface: Someone is cornered when the police come to arrest them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in difficult position' reads as one phrase, but it splits: 'Put in' is the container signal and 'difficult position' alone is the hole. 'Nick' is British slang for arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone honourable has integrity and so deserves esteem and respect.

clue.text: Formerly accommodating Unionist when required

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to another letter inside

parts.note: once means formerly

explanation.surface: A former Unionist turns up whenever needed.
explanation.definitionFit: On cue means at the exact moment needed, as an actor responding to a prompt.

clue.text: Disney film on showing varying sexuality is a hoax

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed beneath, so the sexuality word sits under the hoax

parts.note: bam is an old word for a hoax or to hoax
bi is short for bisexual

explanation.surface: A claim that a Disney film shows varying sexuality is dismissed as a hoax.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambi (1942) is Disney's animated film about a young deer.

clue.text: Flag of European country is cut down

indicators.note: cut down means shortened, losing its final letter

parts.note: Irish means of Ireland

explanation.surface: A European country's flag is being lowered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' reads as a national banner, but a flag is also a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow flag is a wild iris, so flag names this plant.

clue.text: Work by Debussy set in Central America

indicators.note: set in means the answer sits inside the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Debussy piece is staged in Central America.
explanation.definitionFit: La Mer is Debussy's orchestral piece portraying the sea, from 1905.

clue.text: Airmen in court: NCO and an artificer

indicators.note: in places the airmen inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is a body of airmen
an SM, sergeant major, is a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: Airmen, an NCO and a technician stand trial in court.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificer is a skilled worker with their hands, an artisan.

clue.text: Little hesitation probing doctor attached to unpleasant religious institution

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: probing means pushing into another word

parts.note: nasty means unpleasant
er is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A hesitant doctor at a grim religious establishment examines a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Probing' makes NASTERY; 'doctor' is not an anagram signal here but the medical officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A house where monks live under religious vows is a religious institution.

clue.text: Tot with ice? Not the French style

indicators.note: not here means the French article is left out

parts.note: a drink with ice is chilled
le is the French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A tot of spirits with ice is not the French way of drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a measure of spirits, which fits the ice, but it means a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small child, a toddler.
